A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sloth study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original scaling-law evaluations, latent-skill analyses, and downstream predictions using public benchmark data.

after.justification: V4 retains these original analyses and adds held-out predictions of inference-time scaling on MATH.

M1.justification: The core Sloth architecture, objective, and factor transformations are unchanged. Section 4.5 adds an inference-scaling extension: fit question-specific logistic regressions on predicted skills, then aggregate their probabilities into pass@k predictions.

E1.justification: The model inventory, 12 leaderboard benchmarks, and HumanEval, EQ, and AgentBench applications are retained. V4 adds a focused MATH repeated-sampling scenario involving LLaMa 3 Instruct, Gemma, and Pythia, extending evaluation to inference-budget scaling.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain FLOPs variants, Size and Tokens, PCA + FLOPs, and Ruan et al.'s observational method. Brown et al. supplies data and research context for the new experiment but is not evaluated as an additional baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 introduces question-level calibration using seven LLMs and testing on three held-out larger models, with pass@k evaluated across sampling budgets up to 10,000 trials. Existing leaderboard cross-validation and downstream evaluation settings remain as reported in v1.

E4.justification: The new Figure 7 examines how predicted and observed performance curves change with sampling budget for three held-out models. Existing analyses of latent dimension, family intercepts, link functions, and instruction tuning are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. MAE averaging and skill standardization remain unchanged. V4's repeated sampling concerns inference-budget evaluation rather than uncertainty estimation across experimental runs.

E6.justification: V4 adds MATH pass@k curves and revises several downstream fits and loadings. For example, the HumanEval coefficient vector changes from (0.85, -0.02, 0.14) in v1 Figure 7 to (1.35, -0.02, 0.22) in v4 Figure 6. Main and appendix leaderboard MAEs remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V1's identifiability assumptions, Theorem 3.2, and proof are retained as Assumption B.1 and Theorem B.2 in v4. The fitting mathematics and factor-analysis connections also remain unchanged. The new pass@k expression supplies a standard metric calculation.

C1.justification: V4's abstract and contribution list add the claim that Sloth predicts behavior under increased test-time compute. The central claims about efficient cross-family prediction, interpretable latent skills, and parameter identifiability remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V4 adds the interpretation that practitioners can forecast inference-compute gains before training a target model. Section 4.3 shortens qualifications about matching Knowledge across latent dimensions and the detailed d=4 instruction-following behavior. Appendix A's extrapolation and identifiability limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed Huber parameter, Adam optimization, two-hidden-layer link network, PCA construction, and code access remain unchanged. Model-fitting details move from v1 Section 3.3 to v4 Appendix C; no additional implementation settings or access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: V4 adds Allen-Zhu and Li (2024), Brown et al. (2024), and Reckase (2009). It positions the inference-scaling extension against Brown et al. by emphasizing predictions for hypothetical, untrained models. The existing scaling-law and latent-skill positioning is largely retained.

P1.justification: The methodology is substantially reorganized: v1's four subsections become two main-text subsections, with identifiability theory and fitting moved to Appendices B and C. The two-model evaluation discussion is condensed, downstream appendices gain subsections, and a new Section 4.5 changes the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: Main text and references switch to two columns, with widespread figure resizing and relocation. V1 Figure 7 is split into v4 Figures 6 and 29; the standalone two-model summary disappears while its results remain in the appendix. V4 adds the inference-scaling plot and redraws downstream figures.

improvement.justification: Section 4.5 and Figure 7 provide an explicit procedure and held-out evidence for an additional practical application: predicting inference-time scaling before training a larger model. The original benchmark evidence and theory are preserved. Validation covers only three held-out models, and revisions to existing downstream fits are unexplained, so the overall gain is limited.
